name: CISA
note: All CISA cybersecurity advisories, minus medical-device advisories and US election items.

name: Dark Reading
note: DR Global Middle East & Africa section (keyword filter on the main feed). Publishes about weekly.

name: TahawulTech
note: The site has no security category feed (category/security returns 404); the 'security' tag feed is the closest. Trade press: only items naming a threat are kept, and press-release items are dropped (filters.json).

name: Intelligent CIO Middle East
note: Enterprise Security category of the Middle East edition. Trade press: only items naming a threat are kept, and press-release items are dropped (filters.json).

name: Central Bank of Libya
note: Official CBL news (Arabic). Mostly the governor's meetings, so only cyber, fraud and fake-page items are kept.

name: Libya Herald
note: Libyan general news (English); only cybersecurity items are kept.
focus: Bilateral agreements, international tech frameworks and regulatory shifts (cyber items only).

name: Libya Security Monitor
note: Libyan security news, mostly political and military; only cybersecurity items are kept.

name: NISSA
note: National Information Security and Safety Authority (LibyaCERT's parent). Posts rarely (newest Sep 2024 when added); the 60-day age cap keeps old posts off the page.
focus: Architectural cyber defence mandates, national standard alerts and encryption compliance.

name: The Libya Observer
focus: Domestic breaches, public utility outages, local cyber telemetry.
note: Disabled 2026-10-19: the site publishes no RSS/Atom feed (/feed and /rss.xml return 404, no feed link in the page). The pipeline does not scrape pages; enable once a feed exists.

name: LANA (Libyan News Agency)
focus: Official state wire announcements and telecom alert updates.
note: Official state news agency, English feed (an Arabic feed exists at /rss/ar/; one language only, to avoid duplicates). General news, so only cyber items are kept.

name: Security.com Threat Intelligence
focus: APTs and malware campaigns, including those targeting the Libyan energy sector.
note: Symantec / Broadcom threat intelligence blog (global research; Libya-specific items appear only when published).

name: Group-IB
focus: E-payment fraud, mobile banking vulnerabilities and North African banking vectors.
note: Group-IB blog (global research). Its feed's dates have no time zone; they are read as UTC. Spanish-language duplicates (URLs ending -es/) are dropped.

name: NETSCOUT
focus: Volumetric network attack trends and DDoS statistics.
note: Site-wide NETSCOUT feed (mostly product marketing), so only threat items are kept. The per-country DDoS statistics (Cyber Threat Horizon) are a dashboard, not a feed, and cannot be ingested.

name: General Information Authority (GIA) Libya
focus: National data security frameworks and government e-infrastructure defence guidelines.
note: Disabled 2026-10-19: the HTTPS certificate does not match gia.gov.ly, and no feed was found. Certificate checks are never switched off.

name: Africa AI News
focus: North African tech governance, national strategy and regulatory cyber alignment.
note: Africa-wide AI news; only cybersecurity items are kept, and regions come from the headline.

name: Al Jazeera
focus: State infrastructure breaches, regional cyber espionage and mobile spyware.
note: Site-wide English feed (there is no cyber section feed); only cybersecurity items are kept, and regions come from the headline.

name: Al Arabiya
focus: Data leaks, banking security infrastructure and threat attribution in North Africa.
note: Disabled 2026-10-19: the site answers 403 to every non-browser request, including its RSS paths. We do not disguise our User-Agent.

name: Sky News Arabia
focus: National infrastructure vulnerabilities (grids, telecoms) and regional cyber defence.
note: Technology section feed (Arabic); only cybersecurity items are kept.

name: The Cyber Express
note: Disabled 2026-10-19: Cloudflare answers 403 to every non-browser request, including ours. We do not disguise our User-Agent; re-check later or ask the publisher to allow RaqmanaSecurityNews.
